runs.text: A fast git browser for macOS. Open a repository, pick a branch, tag, or commit, walk the tree, read files, page through history, diff, blame, and see the working tree's status. It runs no
process for repository operations: a Rust core built on

reads the object database directly and a native AppKit window shows the result. Reading never writes a byte; every mutation — refs, the index, the working tree, or a remote — passes through a policy that decides what you must confirm first.

kind.text:
cargo install cbindgen --version 0.29.4 --locked
brew install cargo-deny
scripts/install-app.sh    # builds and installs /Applications/RCGit.app
open -a RCGit ~/code/some-repo

runs.text: in the app menu fetches and fast-forwards the checkout it was built from, rebuilds, reinstalls, and relaunches into the new version with the same tabs open.
— its own identifier, its own tabs, an orange icon — for trying changes without disturbing the installed app.
Open a repository with ⌘O, from the Open Recent menu, by typing part of a recent one's name after ⌃R, by dragging its folder onto the window, by passing a path on the command line, or with

. The ref list holds the working tree, branches, remote branches, and tags; selecting one shows its tree, and the app follows along when refs change on disk. History shows the list in the sidebar. Files puts a banner there instead, naming what you browse: click it or press ⌘B to pick from the list in a popover. In Changes the banner names the checked-out branch. Folders load when expanded, files open with syntax highlighting when selected, ⌘F searches the file, ⇧⌘O jumps to a file by fuzzy name. In JavaScript and TypeScript, click an import or a component to open its file. ⌘[ and ⌘] step back and forward through the files, commits, panes, and tabs you went through, across repositories; the toolbar arrows, a two-finger swipe, and a mouse's side buttons do the same.

The Files/History/Changes toggle (⌘1/⌘2/⌘3) switches panes. History pages the commit list as you scroll, and selecting a commit shows the files it changed with a line diff; double-click to browse the tree at that commit. ⌥⌘B blames the open file. The Working Tree row overlays each file's status against
— modified, untracked, ignored, deleted. Right-click a ref to create or delete branches and tags: deleting an unmerged branch, a remote branch, or a tag takes the typed name and writes a backup under
first; a merged branch takes a plain confirm.

The window adapts to its size: narrow windows fold the sidebar away. The file always sits right of the tree, and the tree widens only as far as its rows need, so the file pane takes the rest of the window. Drag the divider and that width is yours from then on. Toggle the sidebar with ⌃⌘S.
The same core ships as a command-line tool for scripts and for measuring:

kind.text:
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- --time ls ~/code/some-repo main src
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- cat ~/code/some-repo v1.2 README.md
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- log ~/code/some-repo -n 10
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- diff ~/code/some-repo v1.1 v1.2 src/main.rs
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- blame ~/code/some-repo main src/main.rs
cargo run --release -p rc-git-cli -- status ~/code/some-repo

runs.text: The core cannot write. The workspace's
rejects the gix and std write, spawn and network entry points it lists at lint time, a test compares

byte for byte before and after every operation, and repositories open in isolated mode so an untrusted checkout cannot pull in configuration from anywhere else. Every mutation — refs, the index, the working tree, or a remote — passes through

, a policy that denies deletions on protected branches outright and decides, per action, whether it runs, needs a confirm, or needs a typed phrase and a backup ref. Deleting a merged branch takes a plain confirm and writes no backup; discarding working changes takes a plain confirm and cannot be undone; dropping a stash takes the word
